senses.gloss: Impossible to break.
examples: These plates are *unbreakable*, which is why we take them camping.
The new phone screen is nearly *unbreakable*.
Kids' cups come in *unbreakable* plastic.

senses.gloss: Impossible to end, break or beat.
examples: The two sisters have an *unbreakable* bond.
For thirty years his home run record looked *unbreakable*.
She made an *unbreakable* promise to her mother.

position: attributive only — before a noun: *unbridled joy*
form: un- + *bridled*, from *bridle*, the straps on a horse's head

senses.gloss: Not held back or controlled at all.
examples: The crowd greeted the team with *unbridled* joy.
*Unbridled* spending got the city into trouble.
He watched the news with *unbridled* anger.

senses.gloss: Going on without a stop or a gap.
examples: We drove through miles of *unbroken* desert.
The team has an *unbroken* streak of eleven wins.
There was an *unbroken* silence in the room.

senses.gloss: Not broken or damaged.
examples: The seal on the box was still *unbroken*.
Only one window was *unbroken* after the storm.

position: both — mostly after a verb: *his collar was unbuttoned*

senses.gloss: With the buttons undone.
examples: His collar was *unbuttoned* and his tie was gone.
She came in wearing an *unbuttoned* coat.
He sat on the porch with his shirt *unbuttoned*.

position: both — mostly after a verb: *that was uncalled-for*; also before a noun: *an uncalled-for remark*
contrast: After a verb many Americans write it as two words, *uncalled for*; the hyphen is normal before a noun.

senses.gloss: Rude or unfair, and not deserved by anything the other person did.
examples: That remark was completely *uncalled-for*.
Firing her over one late report was *uncalled-for*.
He apologized for his *uncalled-for* comments.

senses.gloss: Strange in a way that is hard to explain and a little unsettling.
examples: There was an *uncanny* stillness before the storm.
I had the *uncanny* feeling that we had met before.

senses.gloss: So accurate or so close that it seems impossible.
examples: She has an *uncanny* ability to guess what people are thinking.
The resemblance between the twins is *uncanny*.
His feel for the market is even more *uncanny* than his boss's.

senses.gloss: Not interested in other people's feelings or troubles.
examples: The nurse came across as cold and *uncaring*.
He isn't *uncaring* — he just doesn't know what to say.
They describe the company as an *uncaring* employer.

senses.gloss: Not sorted into any group or category yet.
senses.ru: не отнесённый ни к какой категории
examples: Everything I don't file ends up in an *uncategorized* folder.
Half of last month's expenses are still *uncategorized*.
The app puts *uncategorized* charges at the bottom of the list.

senses.gloss: Going on and on without stopping.
examples: The *unceasing* noise from the highway kept me up.
She showed *unceasing* devotion to her students.
The rain was *unceasing* all weekend.

senses.gloss: Printed, shown or said with nothing cut out.
examples: The streaming service has the *uncensored* version of the movie.
His posts are raw and *uncensored*.
The late show ran the whole interview *uncensored*.

senses.gloss: Not sure about something.
examples: I'm *uncertain* about taking the job.
She was *uncertain* whether to call him back.
Doctors are still *uncertain* of the cause.

senses.gloss: Not known or not settled, and likely to change.
examples: The company faces an *uncertain* future.
Funding for the program is *uncertain*.
In *uncertain* times people save more.

position: both — often after *go*: *the claim went unchallenged*

senses.gloss: Not questioned, argued with or competed against.
examples: His story went *unchallenged* for years.
The mayor ran *unchallenged* in the primary.
That *unchallenged* assumption is where the argument falls apart.

position: both — mostly after a verb: *the price is unchanged*
contrast: *Unchanged* says nothing has changed so far; *unchanging* says it never changes.

senses.gloss: The same as before.
examples: The rules remain *unchanged* this season.
Her plans were *unchanged* by the news.
Ten years later, the town looks *unchanged*.

senses.gloss: Always the same, never changing.
examples: The *unchanging* routine of the farm suited him.
Her position on this has been *unchanging* for years.
Out there the desert sky feels *unchanging*.

senses.gloss: Not the way a person or thing usually is.
examples: That kind of rudeness is *uncharacteristic* of him.
She made an *uncharacteristic* mistake in the last set.
The team's *uncharacteristic* sloppiness cost them the game.

senses.gloss: Unkind in the way it judges someone.
examples: It would be *uncharitable* to say she did it on purpose.
He made an *uncharitable* remark about his neighbor.
That's an *uncharitable* reading of what I wrote.

position: both — almost always before a noun: *uncharted territory*

senses.gloss: New to everyone; never experienced before.
examples: Working from home full-time was *uncharted* territory for the company.
This lawsuit takes the industry into *uncharted* waters.

senses.gloss: Not shown on any map.
examples: Explorers pushed into *uncharted* territory.
The reef lies in *uncharted* waters.

position: both — before a noun (*unchecked growth*) and after *go* or *leave* (*left unchecked*)

senses.gloss: Not stopped or held back by anything.
examples: *Unchecked* development has swallowed the farmland.
If the leak goes *unchecked*, the whole floor will rot.
The fire burned *unchecked* for two days.

senses.gloss: Not looked at or verified.
examples: The numbers went into the report *unchecked*.
*Unchecked* facts are how rumors start.

contrast: *Uncivil* is about rude manners; *uncivilized* is about a whole way of living.

senses.gloss: Rude, especially in a public discussion.
examples: The debate turned *uncivil* in the last ten minutes.
He was never cruel, just a little *uncivil* to waiters.
*Uncivil* comments get deleted from the forum.

contrast: American spelling *uncivilized*, not *uncivilised*. Half the everyday uses are a joke about something unpleasant, like a very early meeting.

senses.gloss: Cruel or crude, below the standard of decent life.
examples: A six a.m. meeting is just *uncivilized*.
He called the conditions in the jail *uncivilized*.
Their *uncivilized* behavior at the game got them thrown out.

senses.gloss: Not picked up or asked for by the owner or winner.
examples: *Unclaimed* bags go to the office downstairs.
The prize money is still *unclaimed*.
The state is holding millions in *unclaimed* property.

contrast: In government and military use it means 'not secret', the opposite of *classified*, not 'not sorted'.

senses.gloss: Not kept secret by the government; open to the public.
examples: The report was released in an *unclassified* version.
Most of the emails were *unclassified*.
He only had access to *unclassified* material.

senses.gloss: Hard to understand, or not known.
examples: The instructions were *unclear*.
It's still *unclear* who will pay for the repairs.
The photo is too *unclear* to read the license plate.

senses.gloss: Not sure about something.
examples: I'm *unclear* on what you want me to do.
They were *unclear* about the deadline.

senses.gloss: With no unnecessary things in it; neat and simple.
examples: Her desk is always *uncluttered*.
The app has a clean, *uncluttered* design.
I like the *uncluttered* look of the new kitchen.

senses.gloss: Not pleasant to sit in, wear or be in.
examples: These shoes are *uncomfortable* after an hour.
The seats in the back row are even more *uncomfortable*.

senses.gloss: Feeling uneasy or embarrassed, or making you feel that way.
examples: I'm *uncomfortable* talking about money.
There was an *uncomfortable* silence after his joke.
She felt *uncomfortable* with the whole arrangement.

senses.gloss: Not yet promised or tied to a side, a plan or a person.
examples: A lot of voters are still *uncommitted*.
He's *uncommitted* to any one plan until he sees the numbers.
The *uncommitted* delegates will decide the nomination.

contrast: *It is not uncommon for...* is a quiet way of saying something happens fairly often.

senses.gloss: Not happening or found often.
examples: Snow in April is *uncommon* here, but it happens.
It's not *uncommon* for flights to be delayed in July.
She has an *uncommon* talent for languages.

senses.gloss: Not willing to talk or to share information.
examples: He gets *uncommunicative* when he's tired.
The witness was *uncommunicative* for the first hour.
She's been distant and *uncommunicative* all week.

senses.gloss: Not good enough to compete with others on price or quality.
examples: Our prices are *uncompetitive* next to the big chains.
High costs have made the plant *uncompetitive*.
An *uncompetitive* bid never gets a second look.

senses.gloss: Simple; without difficult parts.
examples: The recipe is quick and *uncomplicated*.
He wanted an *uncomplicated* life in a small town.
Her surgery was *uncomplicated* and she went home the same day.

senses.gloss: Refusing to change your position or lower your standards.
examples: She is *uncompromising* about safety.
The coach has an *uncompromising* style.
He was *uncompromising* in his demands.

senses.gloss: Not worried about something, or not interested in it.
examples: He seemed *unconcerned* about the deadline.
The cat looked completely *unconcerned*.
They're *unconcerned* with what the neighbors think.

senses.gloss: Given with no conditions or limits at all.
examples: A parent's love should be *unconditional*.
The Allies demanded *unconditional* surrender.
The offer comes with an *unconditional* money-back guarantee.

senses.gloss: Reported but not yet proved to be true.
examples: There are *unconfirmed* reports of a second explosion.
The rumor about the merger is still *unconfirmed*.
We had *unconfirmed* word that the deal had fallen through.

senses.gloss: Having no link to something else.
examples: The two cases are *unconnected*.
His firing was *unconnected* to the audit.
She raised a string of *unconnected* complaints.

contrast: Formal and strong. In law an *unconscionable* contract is one so unfair that a court will not enforce it.

senses.gloss: So unfair or so wrong that no decent person could accept it.
examples: Charging that much for insulin is *unconscionable*.
The delay put an *unconscionable* burden on families.
It would be *unconscionable* to look the other way.

comparison: not gradable — the 'not aware' sense takes *more/most*
contrast: For the hidden part of the mind everyday American English says *subconscious*: *a subconscious fear*.

senses.gloss: Not awake and not able to feel or think, usually after an injury.
examples: The driver was *unconscious* when the medics arrived.
She hit her head and was *unconscious* for a minute.

senses.gloss: Happening without the person knowing it.
examples: The training is about *unconscious* bias.
*Unconscious* habits are the hardest ones to change.

senses.gloss: Not aware of something.
examples: He was *unconscious* of the effect his words had.
They went on talking, *unconscious* of being overheard.

senses.gloss: Against the Constitution, and so not allowed.
examples: The court ruled the law *unconstitutional*.
Critics called the order *unconstitutional*.
An *unconstitutional* statute cannot be enforced.

senses.gloss: Not limited by rules, money or anything else.
examples: Spending was *unconstrained* by any real budget.
She writes with *unconstrained* energy.
*Unconstrained* growth put a strain on the water supply.

senses.gloss: With nobody running against it or arguing against it.
examples: The mayor's seat was *uncontested* this year.
They filed for an *uncontested* divorce.
His claim to the record is *uncontested*.

contrast: *Uncontrolled* means nobody is controlling it; *uncontrollable* means nobody can.

senses.gloss: Impossible to control or stop.
examples: She broke into *uncontrollable* laughter.
The fire was *uncontrollable* by noon.
He has an *uncontrollable* temper.

senses.gloss: Not being watched, limited or treated by anyone.
examples: *Uncontrolled* diabetes can damage your eyes.
The paper compares controlled and *uncontrolled* trials.
*Uncontrolled* spending drained the account in a year.

senses.gloss: Accepted by almost everyone; not causing argument.
examples: The bill was *uncontroversial* and passed in a day.
It's an *uncontroversial* claim among biologists.
He picked an *uncontroversial* topic for the speech.

senses.gloss: Not done the usual way.
examples: They took an *unconventional* route to the top.
Her teaching methods are *unconventional*.
He's an *unconventional* dresser, even for an artist.

contrast: *Unconvinced* describes the listener; *unconvincing* describes the argument.

senses.gloss: Not persuaded that something is true or right.
examples: The jury looked *unconvinced*.
I'm *unconvinced* by his explanation.
She remains *unconvinced* that the plan will work.

senses.gloss: Not good enough to make people believe it.
examples: His excuse was *unconvincing*.
The movie's happy ending is *unconvincing*.
She gave an *unconvincing* smile and looked away.

contrast: For meat and fish Americans usually say *raw*; *uncooked* is the normal word for rice, pasta and dough.

senses.gloss: Not cooked yet.
examples: Measure the rice *uncooked*, not after it swells.
Don't eat *uncooked* cookie dough.
The center of the chicken was still *uncooked*.

contrast: Informal and mostly spoken. The second sense is about behavior, not fashion.

senses.gloss: Not fashionable; embarrassing to be seen with.
examples: Cargo shorts were *uncool* for about a decade.
He was sure his mom's minivan made him *uncool*.

senses.gloss: Not an okay thing to do to someone.
examples: Reading her texts was really *uncool*.
It's *uncool* to bail on your friends at the last minute.

senses.gloss: Not willing to help or to work with others.
examples: The witness was *uncooperative*.

senses.gloss: Clumsy; bad at controlling your own movements.
examples: I was the most *uncoordinated* kid in gym class.

senses.gloss: Not organized so that the parts work together.
examples: The relief effort was slow and *uncoordinated*.

senses.gloss: Not backed up by other evidence or another witness.
examples: The case rests on *uncorroborated* testimony.
His alibi is still *uncorroborated*.
The paper won't run an *uncorroborated* claim.

senses.gloss: Rude and rough in manners or speech.
examples: Talking with your mouth full is *uncouth*.
His *uncouth* jokes cleared the room.
She thought the whole crowd was loud and *uncouth*.

senses.gloss: Accepting something without asking whether it is right or true.
examples: His fans are completely *uncritical*.
*Uncritical* acceptance of a source is how mistakes spread.
She is *uncritical* of anything her own party does.

form: -ed form of *cut*, which does not change

senses.gloss: Shown or printed in full, with nothing taken out.
examples: The DVD has the *uncut* version of the film.
They aired his speech *uncut*.

senses.gloss: Not cut, trimmed or shaped.
examples: He bought an *uncut* diamond at an estate sale.
The lawn was *uncut* for a month.

senses.gloss: Not harmed or broken in any way.
examples: The package arrived *undamaged*.
Only one wall was left *undamaged* by the fire.
*Undamaged* copies of the first edition are rare now.

position: predicative only — after a verb, or at the head of a clause: *Undaunted, she tried again*

senses.gloss: Not discouraged by difficulty or failure.
examples: She was *undaunted* by the first rejection.
*Undaunted*, they set out again at dawn.

contrast: In politics *the undecided* is also a noun: *the undecideds broke late*.

senses.gloss: Not having made a choice yet.
examples: I'm still *undecided* about the trip.
Ten percent of voters are *undecided*.
She was *undecided* whether to major in biology.

senses.gloss: Not settled or finished.
examples: The game was *undecided* until the last minute.
The question of who pays is still *undecided*.

senses.gloss: Not announced or reported to the authorities.
examples: He came home with *undeclared* goods in his suitcase.
It was an *undeclared* war that lasted ten years.
Her major is still *undeclared*.

senses.gloss: Having never lost.
examples: The team went *undefeated* all season.
She's *undefeated* in twelve fights.
They face the last *undefeated* team in the league.

senses.gloss: Not given clear limits or a clear meaning.
examples: His role on the project is *undefined*.

senses.gloss: Needing little effort, or asking little of other people.
examples: It's an *undemanding* job with steady hours.

senses.gloss: Against the idea that people should have an equal say.
examples: Critics called the new rule *undemocratic*.
It's *undemocratic* to count some votes and not others.

senses.gloss: So clearly true that nobody can argue with it.

senses.gloss: Being strongly criticized.

senses.gloss: Being shot at.

position: predicative only — after *be* or *feel*, never before a noun

senses.gloss: A little sick, but not seriously ill.
examples: I'm feeling a little *under the weather* today.

position: attributive only — before a noun; after a verb it is the adverb phrase *under the table*: *they paid him under the table*

position: both — before a noun (*underage drinking*) and after a verb (*he's underage*)
contrast: American English writes it as one word, *underage*, not *under-age*.

senses.gloss: Too young to be legally allowed to do something.
examples: *Underage* drinking is a big problem on campus.

contrast: In *She worked undercover for two years* the word is an adverb, not an adjective.

senses.gloss: Working or done secretly, with a false identity.

contrast: Of countries, Americans now say *developing*; *underdeveloped* sounds dated and rude.

senses.gloss: Working fewer hours than you want, or at a job below your skills.
examples: Many graduates are *underemployed* for years.

position: attributive only — before a noun; after a verb it is the adverb, stressed at the end: *the pipes run underground*

senses.gloss: Below the surface of the ground.
examples: The building has an *underground* parking garage.

senses.gloss: Secret, or outside the official mainstream.
examples: They ran an *underground* newspaper for a year.

senses.gloss: Secret and dishonest.
examples: They won the contract in an *underhanded* way.

position: attributive only — before a noun: *the underlying cause*

senses.gloss: Not getting enough food, or enough of the right food.

senses.gloss: Smaller than the normal or legal size.

senses.gloss: Not having enough workers.

senses.gloss: Natural and easy to sympathize with.

senses.gloss: Able to be understood.

contrast: *An understanding* is also a noun meaning an informal agreement: *we have an understanding*.

senses.gloss: Kind and willing to forgive, because you see why someone acted that way.
examples: My boss was very *understanding* about the delay.
She's an *understanding* teacher.

senses.gloss: Quiet and simple in style, with nothing showy about it.
examples: The dress was elegant and *understated*.
He gave an *understated* performance as the father.

position: both — mostly before a noun; in *swim underwater* it is an adverb

senses.gloss: Below the surface of the water; made for use there.
examples: He bought an *underwater* camera for the trip.
They shot the *underwater* scenes in a tank.

senses.gloss: Owing more on a loan than the thing is worth.
examples: A lot of homeowners were *underwater* on their mortgages in 2009.
She's *underwater* on the car loan and can't sell it.

position: predicative only — after *be* or *get*: *the project is underway*
contrast: Americans usually write it as one word; the older spelling *under way*, as two words, still shows up in careful prose.

senses.gloss: Already started and going on now.
examples: Construction is already *underway*.
The search got *underway* at dawn.
Talks are *underway* to settle the strike.

senses.gloss: Weighing less than is healthy or normal.
examples: The vet says the cat is *underweight*.
He was ten pounds *underweight* at his checkup.
*Underweight* babies need extra monitoring.

contrast: *Undeserved* describes the thing (*undeserved praise*); *undeserving* describes the person (*undeserving of praise*).

senses.gloss: Not earned or fair.
examples: The penalty was completely *undeserved*.

senses.gloss: Not worthy of the help, praise or reward in question.
examples: He felt *undeserving* of the award.

senses.gloss: Not wanted, because it brings harm or trouble.
examples: The drug has some *undesirable* side effects.

The screening weeds out *undesirable* applicants.

senses.gloss: Impossible to find or notice.
examples: The virus was *undetectable* in his blood.
The repair on the frame is almost *undetectable*.

position: both — often after *go*: *the leak went undetected*
contrast: *Undetectable* means nobody could find it; *undetected* means nobody did.

senses.gloss: Not found or noticed, though it was there.
examples: The leak went *undetected* for months.
*Undetected* errors made it into the final report.

senses.gloss: Not yet worked out or decided.
examples: The cause of the fire is still *undetermined*.

position: predicative only — after a verb, or at the head of a clause: *Undeterred, he called again*

senses.gloss: Not stopped or put off by something unpleasant.
examples: She was *undeterred* by the rain and ran anyway.

contrast: *Undeveloped* land has nothing built on it; *underdeveloped* means something grew less than it should have.

senses.gloss: With nothing built on it yet.
examples: They bought ten acres of *undeveloped* land.
The lot next door is still *undeveloped*.

senses.gloss: Not worked on or grown to its full strength.
examples: His talent is real but *undeveloped*.

position: both — often after *go*: *it went undiagnosed for years*

senses.gloss: Not identified by a doctor.
examples: Her celiac disease went *undiagnosed* for years.

senses.gloss: Making someone look silly or lose respect.
examples: There was an *undignified* scramble for the last seats.

senses.gloss: Saying things in a way that offends people.
examples: That was an *undiplomatic* thing to say to a client.

senses.gloss: Not controlling yourself or following the rules.
examples: The team looked *undisciplined* in the first half.

*Undisciplined* spending sank the business.

position: both — mostly before a noun: *an undisclosed amount*

senses.gloss: Deliberately not made public.
examples: The company was sold for an *undisclosed* amount.
He is being treated at an *undisclosed* location.
The terms of the settlement remain *undisclosed*.

senses.gloss: Not found or recognized yet.
examples: Thousands of species are still *undiscovered*.

The error lay *undiscovered* until the audit.

senses.gloss: Accepted by everyone; not argued about.
examples: She's the *undisputed* champion.

senses.gloss: Not touched or moved.
examples: The snow in the yard was *undisturbed*.

senses.gloss: Not interrupted or worried.
examples: He slept *undisturbed* through the storm.
She seemed *undisturbed* by the criticism.

position: attributive only — before a noun: *my undivided attention*

senses.gloss: Whole, given to one thing only.
examples: You have my *undivided* attention.
The plan had the board's *undivided* support.
He gave the project his *undivided* focus for a month.
